definition: In historical theological use, universalism refers to the belief that all sinful beings will ultimately be restored to happiness with God. In this source, it is presented as closely related to apokatastasis.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Apokatastasis; pinned source text

reasons: The packet does not define the term "universalism" itself as the belief that all sinful beings will ultimately be restored to happiness with God; it defines "Apokatastasis" that way.
While the packet states that "Apokatastasis" is "closely connected with UNIVERSALISM (q.v.)," it does not establish that "universalism" has the specific belief-content given in the definition.

The packet defines apokatastasis, not universalism, and only says it is closely connected with universalism; it does not directly support assigning the described doctrine to the term universalism itself.
The definition’s first sentence presents a specific theological meaning for universalism that is not stated in the supplied source, so the requested sense is not fully supported by the packet.
